title: INT8/FP8 kernel paths and dequant fusion for prefill + decode scheduling
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our serving runtime supports mixed-precision execution today (FP16/FP32 fast paths). Customers and internal benchmarks show material cost/throughput gains using INT8 or FP8 quantized kernels, but naive conversion introduces dequant/requant overhead and occasional quality regressions. Goal: implement quantization-friendly kernel selection and scheduling that minimizes dequant copies by fusing dequant + GEMM/attention kernels, and route requests to INT8/FP8 execution paths when accuracy/latency tradeoffs are acceptable.

Objectives:
- Add deterministic kernel-selection heuristics that consider model size, sequence length distribution, batch size, and per-request latency SLO to pick FP16/INT8/FP8/FP32 paths.
- Implement fused dequant->matmul kernels for QKV and attention score compute to avoid intermediate full-precision buffers and extra memory copies.
- Optimize prefill (prefetch/prefill KV cache population) and autoregressive decode scheduling so quantized and mixed-precision work doesn't incur repeated dequant/requant for each decode step.
- Provide microbenchmarks and accuracy validations for asymmetric INT8, per-channel INT8, and FP8 E5M2-like formats across 7B/13B/70B families.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Kernel ABI: introduce an execution descriptor passed to kernels that includes quantization metadata (scale vectors, zero points, per-channel flags) so fused kernels can consume quantized tensors directly. Keep descriptor flat and compact to minimize call overhead.
2) Fused kernels: implement fused dequant(quantized_input) + GEMM + bias + activation for QKV projection and attention matmul. For attention softmax we keep accumulator in FP32/FP16 to preserve numerical stability, but avoid copying inputs back to host memory.
3) Prefill scheduling: perform dequant once during prefill and store cached KV in a compressed quantized layout where possible (for INT8 this is per-channel quantized bytes + scale table). During decode, kernels operate against quantized KV directly and only produce FP16 decode outputs when needed.
4) Fallbacks and rollouts: runtime will maintain per-model compatibility matrix and allow safe canary rollout of INT8/FP8 paths with A/B quality checks and automatic rollback on metric regression.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Implementing fused kernels increases internal runtime complexity and may make debugging harder.
- FP8 modes (dynamic exponent range) can yield large speedups on compatible hardware but are more brittle across model ops; require stricter validation.
- Per-channel quantization reduces accuracy loss but increases metadata and slightly more memory overhead compared to symmetric per-tensor quant.
- On some GPUs (older SMs) the fused path may be slower due to lack of optimized int8 GEMM; need hardware capability checks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fused kernels for QKV and attention implemented and integrated in serving runtime behind config flags.
- End-to-end microbenchmarks: 20-40% token/sec improvement vs FP16 baseline for 7B/13B on INT8 for throughput-oriented batch sizes, and 10-25% latency improvement for small-batch decode on FP8-capable hardware where applicable.
- Accuracy validation: <0.5 BLEU/0.5 perplexity delta on held-out eval set for selected models when using recommended quantization profiles; documented fallback thresholds.
- Canary rollout path in console: toggles, per-route metrics, automatic rollback if quality regressions exceed thresholds.

Dependencies: ENG-9120 (kernel ABI refactor), ENG-9271 (prefill cache refactor), infra provisioning for FP8 instances (ops-requests-2026).
comments: 2026-02-22 - Maya Chen: Spike complete. Implemented prototype fused dequant+matmul for QKV in CUDA for 7B model. Microbenchmarks on p4d show 28% throughput gain (batch=8, seq=1024) vs FP16 baseline. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1842 (WIP).

2026-02-25 - Luca Romano: Reviewed initial PR. Left feedback: (1) split scale table allocation out of hot path, (2) add unit tests for per-channel scale shapes, (3) add runtime hardware capability gating. Filing follow-ups as ENG-9432-sub1 (implementation task) and ENG-9432-sub2 (tests).

2026-03-01 - SRE (Aisha Khan): Observability note — need to add telemetry for kernel path chosen per-request (labels: kernel:int8/kernel:fp8/kernel:fp16) and token-level latency histograms to debug regressions. Added label and dashboard card request: DASH-quant-kernel-paths.

2026-03-05 - Luca Romano: Bench suite updated. Added FP8 pseudo-supported path using emulated FP8 accumulators; results indicate 35% throughput improvement on A100Max vs FP16 for long-prefill workloads but with occasional outlier tokens causing top-k rerank differences. Modeling shows FP8 OK for retrieval-augmented generation but risky for precise summarization prompts.

2026-03-09 - Maya Chen: Decision log: proceed with INT8 fused kernels as default for throughput tier; FP8 support will be opt-in and gated by hardware capability flags and stricter eval. We will store quantized KV cache layout on disk for Dedicated to speed restart. Added release target runtime-1.25.

2026-03-12 - QA (Priya Patel): Runbook updated with validation checklist. End-to-end tests pass for 7B/13B INT8 paths on CI with simulated GPU kernels. Small regressions observed on 70B FP8 path; marking FP8 as experimental and excluding from canary for now.
acceptance_criteria: Implement fused dequant+GEMM kernels for QKV and attention matmul behind feature flags
Runtime chooses quantized path based on model profile, seq length, and SLOs
Prefill stores quantized KV cache usable by decode kernels, avoiding per-token dequant copies
Benchmarks show targeted throughput/latency improvements meeting thresholds
Canary rollout with automatic rollback and telemetry in Console
